proposals.remedy_shape: Not this lane's to apply. The deep-dive block needs the same treatment the ranked table already got: rebuilt on products that exist and figures that have dated sales, or removed. Withdrawn figures are not replaced with new guesses.

proposals.title: HIGH — GA4's newest day is not settled when the nightly snapshot reads it. Sep 17's engagement rate read 8.57% in one night's file and 47.22% in the next. The two fields this lane's FAIL rule depends on (keyEventsYesterday, sessionsYesterday) are taken from that unsettled row.
evidence: Two committed files on the price-data branch, same day, same property, different answers. cc36fb7 (generatedAt 2026-09-18T18:00:17Z, day 2026-09-17), newest daily28 row: {"date":"20260917","sessions":70,"keyEvents":11,"engagementRate":0.08571428571428572,"averageSessionDuration":156.2795861}.

2cbf66f (generatedAt 2026-09-19T12:44:30Z, day 2026-09-18), the SAME Sep 17 row: {"date":"20260917","sessions":72,"keyEvents":12,"engagementRate":0.4722222222222222,"averageSessionDuration":136.01312173611112}.

Engagement rate restated 5.5x (8.57% -> 47.22%); sessions 70 -> 72; key events 11 -> 12. GA4 finishes attributing engagement after it finishes counting sessions, so the ratio moves far more than its inputs.

tools/ga4-snapshot.mjs:113 writes both summary fields straight off the newest row with no settled-day guard: keyEventsYesterday: (rep.daily28.rows.at(-1)||{}).keyEvents, sessionsYesterday: (rep.daily28.rows.at(-1)||{}).sessions.
Line 131 stamps every written file with its own warning: 'Windows end on yesterday (GA4 finishes processing a day ~24h after it ends).' The tool documents the lag and then reads the day inside it.
git grep -in 'provisional' in the clone taken this run returns no hit in any tool, workflow or data file (one unrelated prose hit in data/calls.json). Nothing marks the unsettled row (R7 satisfied).

Today's exposure, unfiled on purpose: the current file's freshest row reads Sep 18 at 4 key events on 54 sessions and a 12.96% engagement rate. On this evidence that is probably not what Sep 18 will say tomorrow. No lane should quote it.
proposals.consequence: The Integrity Watch charter makes ZERO key events on a day with >=30 sessions a FAIL — the Sep 4-16 blackout shape. That test is currently evaluated on the least settled day in the file. A morning where GA4 has attributed nothing yet hands this lane a zero on a healthy day and it files a blackout that does not exist.
proposals.already_cost_something: This produced a wrong finding yesterday. iw-2026-09-19-6(b) filed Sep 17 as 'the 28-day engagement floor, 8.57% against a 45.66% trailing median, -81%'. The settled value is 47.22%, 3% ABOVE the median. See the withdrawal entry below.
proposals.r6: No existing ruling. Nothing in the 139 proposals concerns GA4 processing lag; claude/handoffs/ga4-snapshot-2026-09-18.md and STATE 2026-09-18 section 2 cover the pipeline's construction and first-run verification, not freshness semantics.
proposals.remedy_shape: One file, for the CoS to rule on: either have ga4-snapshot.mjs emit the summary for the newest SETTLED day (day-before-yesterday) alongside the current block, or mark the freshest daily28 row and both *Yesterday fields provisional:true. Then the zero-key-events FAIL is evaluated on a settled day. In the same pass, ga4-history.json's Sep 17 row carries the stale 8.57%-era figures and should be restated from the settled read — it is this lane's trailing-median material, currently seeded with one bad row out of two.

proposals.title: LOW — the board's keywords meta sells the page as '1st Bowman cards 2026' (the base-card category R9 section 3 makes a gate failure), and two prose lines use bare '1st Bowman' as shorthand for the auto.

Prose instance 1 (Holliday entry): 'The headliner of the 2026 Bowman class and the most-chased 1st Bowman in years.'
Prose instance 2 (Kim entry): 'The most expensive 1st Bowman in the entire 2026 class — and he came off the watch tier to take it.'
Every other bare '1st Bowman' on the page is inside the correct phrase 'his 1st Bowman auto'.
audit-terminal's board-autos-only check passes: it reads body copy for the self-description and does not read <meta>.
proposals.why_low: The board's public face is correct where it counts. Title: '1st Bowman Chrome Autos, Ranked and Priced Nightly'. Meta description: 'On-card autos only: not base 1st Bowman Chromes, not graded copies.' The explainer states R9 section 1 verbatim. Both prose instances sit inside entries whose headings and price rows say '1st Bowman Chrome Auto', and keywords meta has been ignored by every major search engine since 2009. No reader is misled.
proposals.why_filed_anyway: The interesting part is the gate's SCOPE: the exact string R9 section 3 names as a FAIL is on the page in a place the gate does not look. The Sep 16 incident Mo caught himself was this category error in this page's public face.
proposals.r6: R9 is doctrine, not a proposal; no item in the 139 covers the keywords meta on any page.

withdrawals.note: Yesterday's finding that 'Sep 17 is the 28-day engagement floor (8.57%, -81% vs a 45.66% median)' was read off an unsettled GA4 row. The settled figure from the next night's snapshot is 47.22% — 3% above the median, entirely ordinary. The finding is withdrawn before it is ruled. It has not yet been appended to data/pipeline.json, so nothing needs to be reversed there. iw-2026-09-19-6(a) — the Singapore cluster — is unaffected and stands on its own evidence (re-read today: 74 sessions, 0.205s average, 38.1% of US sessions, up from 61 / 31.6%). Cause: see iw-2026-09-20-2.
